title: Recording: Same Time Next Year by Wings | 1978
content:
RAK Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney

Wings began recording the song ‘Same Time Next Year’ on 5 May 1978.

The song was written for the 1978 film Same Time, Next Year, directed by Robert Mulligan and starring Alan Alda and Ellen Burstyn. However, it was unused until it became the b-side of Paul McCartney’s 1990 single ‘Put It There’.

The song was commissioned by producer Walter Mirisch to be the main theme of the romantic comedy. McCartney demoed it in June 1977 after viewing an early version of the film.

I wanted a song for the film so I reached Paul through his attorney and asked if he would be interested. The word came back that he would. We sent a rough cut of the picture to him in London, and he recorded a song.
Walter Mirisch
I Thought We Were Making Music, Not History

‘Same Time Next Year’ was the first Wings recording to feature guitarist Laurence Juber and drummer Steve Holley.

The basic track had Paul McCartney on piano, Juber on electric guitar, Denny Laine on bass guitar, Holley on drums, and Linda McCartney on tambourine. Paul then overdubbed lead vocals, and he and Laine added acoustic guitar parts, before they were joined by Linda for backing vocals.

‘Same Time Next Year’ was completed the following day with an orchestral overdub. Ultimately, however, the song was not used in the film, after Robert Mulligan decided that the song gave away key plot points.
